stances_toward.note: NATO ally and Pristina's patron too; Albania is a founding member of Trump's Board of Peace (parliament voted 110 of 140 on 22 Jan 2026, no fee) and the Kushner family's Affinity Partners holds the Sazan/Zvernec concession. Stable because the political tie is intense and the economic tie thin ('extremely weak, despite excellent diplomatic ties'); Albania got only the base 10% tariff and its exports to the US fell about 30% in April 2025; the 2027 NATO summit in Albania is in doubt with US reluctance cited. Bond - affinity: the 1999 Kosovo war made the US Albania's declared ally (per the Wikipedia index).

stances_toward.note: The US is the author of Dayton and still the state's largest security patron on paper, but for Sarajevo it has become a transactional and unreliable one: it lifted sanctions on Dodik and 47 associates on 29 Oct 2025 as a 'responsive measure', told the Council it is 'no longer pursuing nation-building', exerted 'enormous' pressure that ended Schmidt's mandate in May 2026 and lobbied for Zanardi Landi as successor, and Trump Jr. visited Banja Luka in April 2026 (privately). On the other hand the State Department warned Sarajevo against delay on leaving Russian gas and the US-backed Southern Interconnection continues. Bond affinity: the 1995 intervention narrative; the RS leadership paid at least USD 8.9m to Washington lobbyists in 2025-26 and won the sanctions relief it sought.

stances_toward.note: NATO ally and energy patron: the US supplies 67% of Croatia's LNG imports (Plenkovic), Energy Secretary Wright and Plenkovic signed a Balkan gas-infrastructure deal at Dubrovnik on 29 Apr 2026, Washington's OFAC licences decide whether JANAF may ship crude to Serbia, and Croatia joined NATO's PURL arms-for-Ukraine mechanism. Plenkovic told Rubio the alliance was 'excellent' at Munich in Feb 2026 while saying Europe still extends a hand to the US and that how cooperation develops 'remains to be seen' after the tariff and Greenland episodes - a hedge in tone, not a change of grade. Stable, not warming. Bond - affinity: Atlantic alignment since 1990s.

stances_toward.note: Co-members of NATO; no bilateral treaty beyond an Article 98 immunity agreement that the Commission says conflicts with the EU's position. Warming under Mickoski: two Washington visits in less than a month, the 'new normal' language, a February 2025 UNGA vote for the US-backed 'path to peace' text and abstention on the EU-backed Ukraine one, an Atlantic Council event listed for 17 Sep 2026, a US-Turkish joint venture (Bechtel-Enka) building Corridors 8 and 10d. Treated as the patron that can be asked for help with Sofia, though the Council does not answer to Washington. Bond - affinity: the Euro-Atlantic story since 2020 and the Trump channel.

Even Speaker Mandic, from the pro-Serbian bloc, asks for a strategic partnership with the USA (July 2026). stances_toward.note: Strategic dialogue launched in Washington on 17 July 2026; Vučić told Fox News relations were 'dramatically transformed'. Documented friction over NIS sanctions, tariffs and Kosovo. Bond - grievance: the 1999 NATO bombing and the 2008 recognition of Kosovo; about half of Serbians regard the US as an enemy (poll via N1). Structural check: Washington is also Pristina's de facto guarantor (KFOR, Javelins, Board of Peace charter of Jan 2026, see XKX); Belgrade's 'partner' grade rests on transactional gains (strategic dialogue, NIS licences) and on the Trump administration's perceived softness on Kosovo (Vučić, N1, March 2026), not on any shared position on Kosovo.

Bond - affinity: Pristina's founding narrative of US support (Osmani: 'American support has been and remains vital').

relations_to.summary: The Sazan island and Zvernec resort led by Affinity Partners (Jared Kushner) is estimated at USD 1.6bn (EUR 1.4bn in other reports), with 1,500+ residences, a marina and hotels; it was given preliminary approval in 2026 and is under SPAK investigation over the 2024 change of the protected area's status.
relations_to.note: Costs differ between outlets (USD 1.6bn or EUR 1.4bn); the larger figure is kept.
